successCriteria.description: The LeaveRequest model interface is exported from the leave module and imports LeaveRequestStatus from src/shared/types/index.ts; a consumer can import and reference the LeaveRequest type without compile errors.

The ILeaveRequestRepository interface declares five methods with the exact signatures: findById(id): Promise<LeaveRequest | null>, findByEmployee(employeeId): Promise<LeaveRequest[]>, findByStatus(status): Promise<LeaveRequest[]>, create(request: Omit<LeaveRequest, 'id'|'createdAt'|'updatedAt'>): Promise<LeaveRequest>, update(id, data: Partial<LeaveRequest>): Promise<LeaveRequest | null>.

The PgLeaveRequestRepository implementation persists a row on create (INSERT ... RETURNING) and returns the mapped LeaveRequest; findById returns the matching row or null when absent; findByEmployee and findByStatus return filtered arrays (empty array when none match); update applies only provided fields and returns the updated row or null when the id does not exist.

When a database row contains a status value not in the LeaveRequestStatus enum, the row mapper throws an Error naming the invalid value (e.g. "Invalid leave request status from database: <value>"), preventing an invalid enum from propagating to callers.

Every repository method wraps its pool.query call in try/catch and rethrows a new Error with a "Failed to <action>: <message>" prefix, where message is error.message for Error instances or String(error) otherwise — no unhandled promise rejections escape the repository.

Jest unit tests at tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.repository.test.ts mock the db connection module and cover, per method: a success case returning the expected mapped model, a not-found/empty case (null or empty array), and an error case asserting the wrapped Error message; the test suite passes under npx jest.

constraints: No use of the `any` type anywhere in the leave module files; use `unknown` with type guards/casts (e.g. `error: unknown` in catch blocks, `Record<string, unknown>` for DB rows) per HARNESS.json constraint no-any.

All database access for leave requests goes through the repository class implementing ILeaveRequestRepository; no inline SQL or direct pool.query calls outside the repository implementation (GP-001, HARNESS.json no-direct-db-outside-repository).

All SQL queries must use parameterized placeholders ($1, $2, ...) with values passed as a separate array; no string interpolation or concatenation of user-supplied values into SQL text to prevent SQL injection.

Code must compile under strict TypeScript (noImplicitAny, strictNullChecks); nullable fields (reason, approvedBy, approvedAt) must be typed as `| undefined` / `| null` and handled explicitly, never assumed non-null.

The repository obtains the database connection via a direct module-level import of the singleton `pool` from src/shared/db/connection.ts (no constructor injection), matching the balance repository convention.
Every async repository method catches errors from pool.query and rethrows a wrapped Error; no async method can reject with a raw pg error or an unhandled rejection (GP-006).
outOfScope: LeaveService, state-machine transitions (DRAFT→SUBMITTED→APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED), balance sufficiency checks (BR-001), and manager approval logic (BR-002) — these belong to Phase 6 and are not part of this data-layer phase.
LeaveController, leaveRoutes, Fastify route registration, and any HTTP endpoint surface — these belong to Phase 7 and are out of scope for this phase.
AuditLog recording for leave request state changes (GP-002) — the audit module and its integration into the leave workflow belong to Phases 8–9 and are not part of this repository-only phase.
Notification service and any email/in-app notification on submission, approval, rejection, or cancellation — belongs to Phase 10 and is out of scope.

Creating or altering the leave_requests table schema (Knex migrations) — the table is assumed to already exist with the reconciled snake_case columns; this phase only implements the data-access layer against it.

entityInvariants.invariant: The status field of any LeaveRequest returned by the repository must always be a member of the LeaveRequestStatus enum (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED); a row whose status is not in this set must never be returned to a caller — the mapper must throw instead.

All date-typed fields (startDate, endDate, createdAt, updatedAt) on a returned LeaveRequest must be JavaScript Date instances constructed from the database column values; approvedAt must be a Date when present or null when the column is null — never a raw string.

The create operation accepts only the caller-supplied fields (Omit<LeaveRequest, 'id'|'createdAt'|'updatedAt'>); id, createdAt, and updatedAt are always generated by the database (RETURNING clause) and never set from caller input.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns null when no row matches the id; throws a wrapped Error ("Failed to find leave request by id: <message>") on database failure.
Returns an empty array (not null) when no rows match the employeeId; throws a wrapped Error on database failure.
Returns an empty array when no rows match the given status; throws a wrapped Error on database failure.
Throws a wrapped Error ("Failed to create leave request: <message>") on database failure (e.g. FK violation for unknown employee_id or leave_policy_id); never returns null on success.

interfaceConstraints.operation: update(id: string, data: Partial<LeaveRequest>): Promise<LeaveRequest | null>
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns null without issuing a query when the partial data is empty (no fields to set); returns null when the id does not exist (zero rows returned); throws a wrapped Error on database failure.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The leave repository's try/catch error wrapping must match the balance repository pattern: `catch (error: unknown) { const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error); throw new Error(\`Failed to <action>: ${message}\`); }` — same structure, same message format.

The leave repository must validate the status column against a `ReadonlySet<string>` built from `Object.values(LeaveRequestStatus)`, throwing `Invalid leave request status from database: <value>` on mismatch — mirroring the balance repository's `VALID_STATUSES` set and `mapRowToBalance` validation.

The update method must return null without querying when the partial data has no settable fields (setClauses.length === 0), matching the balance repository's self-contained `return null` convention (not delegating to findById as the policy repository does).

All SELECT and RETURNING clauses must enumerate the explicit snake_case column list (id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at) rather than using `SELECT *`, matching the balance and policy repository conventions.

The LeaveRequestStatus enum imported and validated against must be the one exported from src/shared/types/index.ts (DRAFT='DRAFT', SUBMITTED='SUBMITTED', APPROVED='APPROVED', REJECTED='REJECTED', CANCELLED='CANCELLED'); the model and repository must import from this exact path, not redefine the enum.

The leave repository test must follow the balance test structure: jest.mock on the connection module, a sampleRow fixture with snake_case columns, an expectedModel fixture with camelCase fields and Date instances, and per-method describe blocks covering success/not-found/error cases.

integrationPoints.why: The leave model and repository import LeaveRequestStatus from the shared types module; this is the source of truth for the status enum values used in validation.
The repository imports the singleton `pool` from the shared DB connection module to execute all SQL queries; this is the only database access point.

The repository reads from and writes to the leave_requests table with snake_case columns (id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at); FKs reference employees.id and leave_policies.id.

The ILeaveRequestRepository interface and PgLeaveRequestRepository implementation produced in this phase are the data-access contract that the future LeaveService will depend on for all leave request persistence operations.
